source_ref: DATA: figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.3122734 (Kotsou 2016, 'SCS: Self-Compassion Scale, validation of the French version', CC BY 4.0 per api.figshare.com/v2/articles/3122734), single file SCSdata.xls (sheet 'Etude 1', 1554 rows x 88 cols, sha256 8dd0bf0ab67d34e67b371662769184981be91850f8fffe8c3f4464f627cd2c29); bare headers PANAS1..PANAS20, cells stored as strings A1..A5, no labels at any level. PAPER: Kotsou I, Leys C (2016) 'Self-Compassion Scale (SCS): Psychometric Properties of The French Translation and Its Relations with Psychological Well-Being, Affect and Depression', PLOS ONE 11(4):e0152880, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0152880 (CC BY), PMC4831759; full text via Europe PMC fullTextXML and supplements S1-S5 + table images via the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint. WORDING: Watson D, Clark LA, Tellegen A (1988) J Pers Soc Psychol 54(6):1063-1070, doi:10.1037/0022-3514.54.6.1063 -- the 20 canonical adjectives in printed order and the five canonical anchors. Processing script data/kotsou_2016_scs_french.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/kotsou_2016_panas/.
note: PASS with real caveats (canonical English substitute for a French administration; within-valence order not independently pinned). STEP 3b CLEAN: the paper's Measures section describes 'The PANAS ... a 20-item tool that measures two dimensions of mood: Positive Affect (PA, 10 items, alpha = .84) and Negative affect (NA, 10 items, alpha = .89)' on 5-point scales, i.e. the original 20-item PANAS (not PANAS-X or I-PANAS-SF); live table has 20 items, resp 1-5. CODE DERIVATION: pattern 1 -- data/kotsou_2016_scs_french.py selects columns matching ^PANAS\d+$ by name and melts them, so the IRW code IS the xls header; resp is the digit of the source string A1..A5 (A{k} -> k), asserted in the script. TEXT: the deposit carries no item text (bare headers, .xls, no comments/labels); the paper quotes only two example adjectives ('Proud' for PA, 'Nervous' for NA) and supplements hold none (S1 SCS factor pattern, S2 French SCS questionnaire only, S3 SCS item correlation matrix, S4 SCS subscale correlations, S5 ethics waiver). So the 20 adjectives are Watson et al.'s canonical English assigned by printed position PANASn = canonical item n -> mapping_basis=reconstructed. LANGUAGE: administered in French (French-speaking community sample; the paper says a French validation of the PANAS was used but its citation is garbled -- '[27]. French validation)' -- and ref 27 is actually Blais et al.'s French SWLS, so the French PANAS version is not identified). No French PANAS wording exists in the deposit or the paper's supplements, so per SKILL.md the fallback applies: canonical English in the base fields, language=French, no _translated columns, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english. The French adaptation's item order is ASSUMED to follow Watson's; the data support that only to the level of valence class (below). INSTRUCTIONS: left blank -- neither paper nor deposit reproduces the instruction paragraph; the paper paraphrases the timeframe as rating 'the degree to which they generally feel specific emotions', which is not imported (medvedev_2018_pan precedent). ANCHORS: paper says only '5-point Likert scales'; canonical Watson anchors shipped (1 very slightly or not at all, 2 a little, 3 moderately, 4 quite a bit, 5 extremely). Direction checked against data: A1->1 lowest is consistent with PANAS8 'Hostile' as the least-endorsed item (mean 1.81, 50.6% at 1) and mean PA items > NA items; the reverse would put 'Hostile' at mean 4.19 in a community sample. Every item uses all five levels (min cell 21). RIGHTS: no block. instrument_rights_register.csv carries verdict=ship for the Watson/Clark/Tellegen PANAS (the 'bare copyright notice on the article' case); applied, not re-derived; no register row written. Deposit CC BY 4.0. VERIFICATION (verify_kotsou_2016_panas.R, PASS; Step 5b PARTIAL): every one of the 20 codes correlates more with its canonical valence block than the other (e.g. PANAS9 rPA .43 vs rNA -.20; PANAS2 rPA -.18 vs rNA .48; weakest PANAS3 'Excited' .20 vs .15 and PANAS12 'Alert' .27 vs .02); canonical-split subscales reproduce the paper's Table 1: PA M 3.372 vs 3.37, SD .656 vs .65, alpha .835 vs .84; NA M 2.463 vs 2.46, alpha .893 vs .89. DISCREPANCY: NA SD computed 0.833 vs published .69 -- mean and alpha match exactly, so this looks like a reporting error in Table 1 rather than a mapping or data defect; not resolved. NOT established: which adjective is which WITHIN a valence block.
public_note: Item and response-option wording is the standard English PANAS (Watson, Clark & Tellegen, 1988) assigned by item number, standing in for the French version respondents actually read, which the source does not publish; the data confirm each item's positive/negative affect grouping but not which adjective is which within a group, and the instructions are not published and are left blank.
